name: Multiple sulfatase deficiency / metachromatic-spectrum leukodystrophy variant

reference.source: Neurology and inborn-errors-of-metabolism textbooks with peer-reviewed reviews
clinicalPearls: Autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic variants in SUMF1, encoding the formylglycine-generating enzyme required to activate all sulfatases
Because every sulfatase is deficient, the phenotype combines metachromatic leukodystrophy with features of several mucopolysaccharidoses and X-linked ichthyosis
Neurological picture overlaps late-infantile metachromatic leukodystrophy, with regression of milestones, spasticity, and peripheral neuropathy
Somatic clues include coarse facial features, skeletal dysostosis, organomegaly, and ichthyotic skin, distinguishing it from isolated arylsulfatase A deficiency
Peripheral demyelinating neuropathy with slowed nerve conduction is a useful supportive finding, mirroring classic metachromatic leukodystrophy
MRI demonstrates symmetrical, confluent periventricular white-matter signal change, sometimes with a tigroid or leopard-skin sparing pattern within the affected white matter
Biochemical hallmark is combined deficiency of multiple sulfatases with raised urinary glycosaminoglycans and sulfatides
Diagnosis is confirmed by demonstrating deficient activity of several sulfatases and by SUMF1 genetic testing; no curative therapy exists
reference.pathophysiology: In multiple sulfatase deficiency, biallelic variants in SUMF1 impair the formylglycine-generating enzyme that performs a post-translational modification essential for the catalytic activity of every sulfatase. As a result all sulfatases are simultaneously deficient, so sulfated substrates accumulate across multiple pathways: sulfatides build up in myelin (as in metachromatic leukodystrophy), glycosaminoglycans accumulate (as in mucopolysaccharidoses), and cholesterol sulfate accumulates in skin (as in X-linked ichthyosis). The combined storage produces central and peripheral demyelination alongside the somatic, skeletal, and dermatological features of the overlapping disorders.
additionalDifferentials: Classic metachromatic leukodystrophy from isolated arylsulfatase A deficiency
X-linked ichthyosis considered in isolation for the skin findings
additionalInvestigations: Assay of multiple sulfatase activities demonstrating combined deficiency
Nerve conduction studies to document demyelinating peripheral neuropathy
Brain MRI to characterise the confluent periventricular leukodystrophy pattern
SUMF1 molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
redFlags: Rapid developmental regression with loss of previously acquired skills
Progressive bulbar dysfunction with aspiration risk
Airway compromise from combined storage-related upper-airway and skeletal changes
reference.prognosis: The disorder is progressive with a poor prognosis, especially in neonatal and late-infantile presentations, which typically lead to severe disability and early death; later-onset forms progress more slowly but remain relentless. No disease-modifying treatment is currently available.
pitfalls: Testing only arylsulfatase A and diagnosing isolated metachromatic leukodystrophy while missing the combined deficiency
Overlooking the somatic and dermatological clues (coarse features, ichthyosis, dysostosis) that point away from an isolated leukodystrophy
Attributing the neuropathy solely to a central process and not testing nerve conduction
Failing to recognise the multisystem nature when planning surveillance and supportive care
references: GeneReviews / standard inborn-errors-of-metabolism references on Multiple Sulfatase Deficiency
Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
management: Provide supportive care as no therapy corrects the combined sulfatase deficiency, directing treatment at the individual manifestations
Control seizures with antiepileptic drugs and manage spasticity with antispasticity agents and physiotherapy
Support feeding and nutrition and manage respiratory secretions as neurological regression advances
Treat the ichthyotic skin with emollients and keratolytic agents
Undertake surveillance for the mucopolysaccharidosis-type complications, including skeletal, cardiac valve, hearing, ophthalmic, and organomegaly monitoring
Coordinate multidisciplinary care with early involvement of palliative services
Offer genetic counselling and family screening given autosomal recessive inheritance of SUMF1 variants
